question: Which Delhi Sultan appointed people from humble professions to high administrative posts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Tughlaq.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक) ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1325 to 1351 AD and was known for his novel yet impractical experiments.

• Unlike earlier Sultans who reserved high posts for the nobility, he appointed people from low and humble professions (barbers, cooks, weavers, gardeners) to high administrative offices.

• This break from the traditional Turkish aristocracy is one reason his nobles grew disaffected.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• His famous experiments include the transfer of capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token (bronze/copper) currency.

• He belonged to the Tughlaq dynasty, founded by his father Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320.

• The traveller Ibn Battuta visited India during his reign and was appointed Qazi of Delhi.

NOTE

• Ruknuddin Firuz (Option 2): A short-lived Slave (Mamluk) dynasty ruler, son of Iltutmish, deposed in 1236.

• Minhaj-us-Siraj (Option 3): A 13th-century historian, author of *Tabaqat-i-Nasiri*, not a Sultan.

• Ghiyasuddin Balban (Option 4): Slave dynasty Sultan who upheld the prestige of the crown and the theory of kingship, favouring high-born nobles.

question: Which of the following regions was annexed by Akbar in 1568?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chittor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chittor (चित्तौड़), the Mewar stronghold, was besieged and captured by Akbar in 1567–1568 AD.

• The fort was defended by Jaimal and Patta (Fatta) on behalf of Rana Udai Singh II, who had retreated to the hills.

• The fall of Chittor was a major step in Akbar's expansion into Rajputana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Akbar later erected statues of Jaimal and Patta on elephants at the gate of Agra Fort to honour their bravery.

• Mewar continued its resistance under Rana Pratap, famously at the Battle of Haldighati (1576).

• Akbar's reign (1556–1605) marked the consolidation and expansion of the Mughal Empire.

NOTE

• Bengal (Option 1): Annexed by Akbar in 1576 after the Battle of Rajmahal against Daud Khan Karrani.

• Gujarat (Option 2): Conquered by Akbar in 1572–1573; to commemorate it he built the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri.

• Orissa (Option 4): Brought under Mughal control later, in the 1590s, by Akbar's general Man Singh.

question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from Japan?
option_2: Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme court
solution_text:
The correct answer is Concept of “procedure established by Law”.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The “procedure established by law” (विधि द्वारा स्थापित प्रक्रिया) under Article 21 is borrowed from the Constitution of Japan.

• It means a law duly enacted by the legislature is valid if it has followed the correct procedure, differing from the American “due process of law”.

• The Indian Constitution is often called a “bag of borrowings” as it draws features from many countries.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In the *Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India* (1978) case, the Supreme Court broadened Article 21 to virtually include “due process”.

• From Japan, India adopted the procedure established by law; from the USA, Fundamental Rights and Judicial Review.

• The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950.

NOTE

• Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (Option 2): Borrowed from Canada (Article 143).

• Judicial review (Option 3): Borrowed from the United States of America.

• Impeachment of the President (Option 4): Borrowed from the United States of America.

question: Which of the following country is one of the founding member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kazakhstan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (शंघाई सहयोग संगठन) was founded on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai, China.

• Its six founding members were China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

• Kazakhstan is therefore a founding member of the SCO.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The SCO grew out of the earlier Shanghai Five grouping (1996), which excluded Uzbekistan.

• Its headquarters (Secretariat) is located in Beijing, China.

• The SCO focuses on security, counter-terrorism, economic and cultural cooperation.

NOTE

• Iran (Option 1): Became a full member of the SCO in 2023, not a founder.

• India (Option 2): Joined the SCO as a full member in 2017 (along with Pakistan).

• Pakistan (Option 3): Also became a full member in 2017, not a founding member.

question: The International Court of Justice is located at _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hague.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The International Court of Justice / ICJ (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय न्यायालय) is located at The Hague, Netherlands, in the Peace Palace.

• It is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, established in 1945.

• It is the only principal UN organ not located in New York.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the UN General Assembly and Security Council.

• It settles legal disputes between states and gives advisory opinions on legal questions.

• Justice Dalveer Bhandari of India is a serving judge of the ICJ.

NOTE

• New York (Option 2): Headquarters of the United Nations (General Assembly, Security Council, Secretariat).

• Beijing (Option 3): Capital of China; hosts the SCO Secretariat, not the ICJ.

• Paris (Option 4): Headquarters of UNESCO and the OECD.

question: Harmanpreet Singh has been awarded the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2024. He is associated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hockey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Harmanpreet Singh (हरमनप्रीत सिंह) is associated with the sport of Hockey (हॉकी).

• He is the captain of the Indian men's hockey team and a specialist drag-flicker.

• He received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2024, India's highest sporting honour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Harmanpreet captained India to the bronze medal at the Paris 2024 Olympics and was the top scorer.

• India also won a bronze at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, ending a 41-year Olympic medal drought in hockey.

• The Khel Ratna Award is named after the legendary hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand.

NOTE

• Chess (Option 1): India's top figures include Grandmasters D. Gukesh and Viswanathan Anand.

• Shooting (Option 3): Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals in shooting at Paris 2024 and shared the 2024 Khel Ratna.

• Para-Athletics (Option 4): Praveen Kumar (high jump) was among the 2024 Khel Ratna awardees from para-athletics.

question: In September 2024, the Supreme Court has affirmed that the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, _____, applies to all women in India regardless of their religion or social background.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (घरेलू हिंसा से महिला संरक्षण अधिनियम) was enacted in 2005 and came into force in 2006.

• In September 2024, the Supreme Court affirmed it applies to all women in India irrespective of religion or social background.

• It provides civil remedies to women facing domestic violence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Act recognises physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse.

• It provides for Protection Officers, protection orders, residence orders and monetary relief.

• A woman in a “shared household” has the right to reside there under the Act.

NOTE

• 2001 (Option 1): No Domestic Violence Act; the National Policy for Empowerment of Women was framed in 2001.

• 2003 (Option 2): Incorrect year; not associated with this Act.

• 2007 (Option 4): Year the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was passed, not the DV Act.

question: Launched in 2025, what is the main objective of the Gyan Bharatam Mission?
option_2: To survey, document, and conserve India’s manuscript heritage
solution_text:
The correct answer is To survey, document, and conserve India’s manuscript heritage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gyan Bharatam Mission (ज्ञान भारतम मिशन) was announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 to survey, document, and conserve India's manuscript heritage.

• It aims to cover more than one crore manuscripts held in academic, museum, library and private collections.

• It builds upon and revamps the earlier National Mission for Manuscripts (2003).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The mission is implemented under the Ministry of Culture.

• It seeks to create a national digital repository and promote scholarly access to ancient texts.

• It combines traditional wisdom with modern digital technology for preservation.

NOTE

• To digitize historical paintings (Option 1): Not the focus; the mission concerns manuscripts, not paintings.

• To fund new book publications (Option 3): Incorrect; it deals with preserving old manuscripts, not funding new books.

• To promote modern literature (Option 4): Incorrect; the mission's aim is heritage conservation, not modern literature.

question: In the World Air Quality Report 2024, what is India's rank among the most polluted countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the World Air Quality Report 2024 (विश्व वायु गुणवत्ता रिपोर्ट 2024) by IQAir, India ranked 5th among the most polluted countries.

• India had slipped from 3rd (in 2023) to 5th, but its air quality still remained far above WHO limits.

• The report is based on PM2.5 concentration data.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The top four most polluted countries in 2024 were Chad, Bangladesh, Pakistan and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

• Byrnihat (Meghalaya/Assam border) was among the most polluted cities globally; Delhi remained the most polluted capital.

• Only seven countries met the WHO annual PM2.5 guideline in 2024.

NOTE

• 3rd (Option 1): India's rank in the 2023 report, not 2024.

• 9th (Option 3): Incorrect rank; not India's position in the 2024 report.

• 46th (Option 4): Incorrect; far from India's actual ranking among polluted countries.

question: NITI Aayog has released the first School Education Quality Index in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2019.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NITI Aayog (नीति आयोग) released the first School Education Quality Index (SEQI) in 2019.

• It ranked states and UTs on the quality of school education based on learning outcomes, access, equity and governance.

• It aimed to drive improvements through competitive and cooperative federalism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

• Among larger states, Kerala topped the first SEQI rankings.

• NITI Aayog also releases the SDG India Index and the Health Index.

NOTE

• 2016 (Option 2): Incorrect; SEQI was not launched this year.

• 2015 (Option 3): The year NITI Aayog itself was set up, not when SEQI was released.

• 2024 (Option 4): Incorrect; SEQI was first released well before this year.

question: Which of the following is the second largest habitat of the One-Horned Rhinoceros in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaldapara National Park.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jaldapara National Park (जलदापाड़ा राष्ट्रीय उद्यान) in West Bengal is the second largest habitat of the One-Horned Rhinoceros in India.

• It is located in the Alipurduar district, on the banks of the Torsa River.

• Kaziranga in Assam holds the largest population of the Indian rhino.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The One-Horned Rhinoceros (*Rhinoceros unicornis*) is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.

• Other rhino habitats in India include Pobitora, Orang and Manas in Assam.

• Jaldapara was declared a national park in 2014.

NOTE

• Kaziranga National Park (Option 1): In Assam; a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the largest rhino habitat, not second.

• Gir National Park (Option 3): In Gujarat; the only home of the Asiatic Lion, not rhinos.

• Kanha National Park (Option 4): In Madhya Pradesh; known for tigers and the barasingha (swamp deer).

question: India started working in space research with the launch of a meteorological rocket in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1963.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India began space research with the launch of its first sounding (meteorological) rocket (मौसम संबंधी रॉकेट) on 21 November 1963.

• It was launched from Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

• This marked the formal beginning of India's space programme.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The programme was pioneered under Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, regarded as the father of the Indian space programme.

• INCOSPAR (Indian National Committee for Space Research) preceded ISRO, which was formed in 1969.

• The first rocket launched was an American Nike-Apache.

NOTE

• 1952 (Option 1): Incorrect; India's space efforts had not yet begun.

• 1957 (Option 2): Year the USSR launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, not related to India.

• 1984 (Option 4): Year Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space aboard a Soviet mission.

question: The Satish Dhawan Space Centre is located in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sriharikota.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Satish Dhawan Space Centre / SDSC (सतीश धवन अंतरिक्ष केंद्र) is located at Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh.

• It is ISRO's primary spaceport, used for launching satellites and vehicles like PSLV and GSLV.

• It is situated on a barrier island on the Bay of Bengal coast.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It was renamed in 2002 after Satish Dhawan, a former Chairman of ISRO.

• The Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan missions were launched from here.

• It has two active launch pads for orbital missions.

NOTE

• Bhopal (Option 1): Capital of Madhya Pradesh; not an ISRO launch site.

• Ahmedabad (Option 2): Location of the Space Applications Centre (SAC) and Physical Research Laboratory, not the launch centre.

• Chennai (Option 3): A major metropolis in Tamil Nadu; not the location of the spaceport.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding gaseous state?
I. In this state, the particles move about randomly at high speed
II. Gases are highly compressible
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the gaseous state (गैसीय अवस्था), particles are far apart and move about randomly at high speed (Statement I is correct).

• Because of large intermolecular spaces, gases are highly compressible (Statement II is correct).

• Hence both statements are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gases have neither fixed shape nor fixed volume and exert pressure on the walls of their container.

• High compressibility allows large volumes of gas (e.g., CNG, LPG) to be stored in small cylinders.

• Intermolecular forces of attraction are weakest in gases compared to liquids and solids.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement II is also true.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement I is also true.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements accurately describe gases.

question: In August 2025, DRDO tested ‘Sudarshan Chakra’ project related to _____
solution_text:
The correct answer is Air Defence Laser System.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In August 2025, DRDO conducted tests under Mission ‘Sudarshan Chakra’ (सुदर्शन चक्र), related to an air defence system, including directed-energy/laser weapons.

• It is envisioned as an indigenous, layered air-and-missile defence shield (an ‘Iron Dome’ style system) targeted for 2035.

• The successful maiden test of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) advanced this mission.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mission Sudarshan Chakra was announced by PM Narendra Modi during the Independence Day (15 August) 2025 address.

• DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation) is the R&D wing of the Ministry of Defence, set up in 1958.

• The system is designed to detect, track and neutralise aerial threats like drones, missiles and aircraft.

NOTE

• Satellite (Option 1): Space assets are handled largely by ISRO and DRDO's defence-space programmes, not this project.

• Nuclear Reactor (Option 2): Managed by the Department of Atomic Energy, unrelated to Sudarshan Chakra.

• Submarine (Option 3): India's submarine programme includes the INS Arihant class; not linked to this air-defence mission.

question: Under whose leadership did the Khalsa revolt against the Mughal rule after the death of Guru Gobind Singh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banda Bahadur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Banda Singh Bahadur (बंदा बहादुर) led the Khalsa in revolt against Mughal rule after the death of Guru Gobind Singh in 1708.

• He established Sikh authority in the region and struck coins in the name of the Gurus.

• He captured Sirhind in 1710 after the Battle of Chappar Chiri.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Originally an ascetic named Madho Das, he was blessed and commissioned by Guru Gobind Singh at Nanded.

• He was captured by the Mughals and executed at Delhi in 1716 under Emperor Farrukhsiyar.

• He is remembered as the first Sikh to establish a sovereign Sikh state.

NOTE

• Chattar Singh Attriwal (Option 1): A Sikh leader during the Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49), a much later period.

• Duleep Singh (Option 3): The last Maharaja of the Sikh Empire, son of Ranjit Singh, in the 19th century.

• Udai Singh (Option 4): Rana Udai Singh II of Mewar, a Rajput ruler, unrelated to the Khalsa.

question: The rupee was made convertible on the current account of the balance of payments in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is August 1994.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian rupee was made fully convertible on the current account (चालू खाते में परिवर्तनीय) in August 1994.

• India accepted the obligations of Article VIII of the IMF's Articles of Agreement at this time.

• This was part of the economic liberalisation reforms of the early 1990s.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Current account convertibility covers trade, services, remittances and interest payments.

• The rupee was made partially convertible earlier under the LERMS (Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System) in 1992.

• The capital account is still only partially convertible in India.

NOTE

• November 1994 (Option 1): Incorrect month; convertibility was declared in August 1994.

• January 1995 (Option 3): Incorrect; falls after the actual date of current account convertibility.

• March 1995 (Option 4): Incorrect; not associated with rupee current-account convertibility.

question: How many members can the President of India nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The President of India (भारत के राष्ट्रपति) can nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

• These members are nominated for their special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

• This is provided under Article 80 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated).

• Nominated members can vote in all matters except the election of the President (they can vote in the Vice-President's election).

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution.

NOTE

• 10 (Option 1): Incorrect number; not the strength of nominated members in the Rajya Sabha.

• 14 (Option 3): Incorrect; exceeds the constitutional limit of 12 nominations.

• 15 (Option 4): Incorrect; not the prescribed number of Presidential nominees.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the election of Vice president of India?
I. He should have completed 35 years of age.
II. He should be qualified for election as a member of the Council of States.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To be elected Vice-President of India (भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति), a person must have completed 35 years of age (Statement I correct).

• He must also be qualified for election as a member of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) (Statement II correct).

• Both eligibility conditions are laid down in Article 66 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses of Parliament (members of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).

• The election is held through proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote and secret ballot.

• The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement II is also a valid qualification.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, since Statement I is also a valid qualification.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both are genuine constitutional requirements.

question: The AMUL milk cooperative was set up in _____
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1946.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The AMUL (अमूल) milk cooperative was set up in 1946 as the Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers' Union at Anand, Gujarat.

• It was formed to protect dairy farmers from exploitation by middlemen.

• AMUL stands for Anand Milk Union Limited.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Its founding is linked to leaders Tribhuvandas Patel and later Dr. Verghese Kurien, the “Father of the White Revolution”.

• AMUL inspired Operation Flood (1970), which made India the world's largest milk producer.

• AMUL is managed by the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF).

NOTE

• 1957 (Option 2): Incorrect; not the founding year of AMUL.

• 1979 (Option 3): Year the Institute of Rural Management Anand (IRMA) was established, not AMUL.

• 1992 (Option 4): Incorrect; far later than AMUL's establishment.

question: In which of the following state, iron ore occurs in a series of hill ranges in Sundergarh, Mayurbhanj and Jhar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Odisha (ओडिशा), iron ore occurs in a series of hill ranges in Sundergarh, Mayurbhanj and Keonjhar (Jhar) districts.

• Odisha is the largest producer of iron ore in India.

• The ore here is mainly high-grade haematite.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Important iron ore mines in Odisha include Gurumahisani, Sulaipat and Badampahar (Mayurbhanj) and Kiriburu, Meghahatuburu and Bonai ranges.

• India's other major iron-ore states are Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Jharkhand.

• Iron ore is a key raw material for the iron and steel industry.

NOTE

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): Has some iron ore (e.g., Anantapur, Kadapa), but not the Sundergarh-Mayurbhanj belt.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Iron ore occurs in Salem district, but not in these named hill ranges.

• Meghalaya (Option 3): Known for coal and limestone, not for major iron-ore hill ranges.

question: Why do single-celled organisms do not need specific organs for taking in food, exchanging gases, or removing wastes?
option_2: Their entire surface is in contact with the environment
option_3: They have a protective wall around them
option_4: They do not perform these functions
solution_text:
The correct answer is Their entire surface is in contact with the environment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In single-celled (unicellular) organisms (एककोशिकीय जीव), the entire body surface is in contact with the environment.

• Hence food intake, gas exchange and waste removal can occur directly across the surface by simple diffusion.

• There is therefore no need for specialised organs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Examples of unicellular organisms include *Amoeba*, *Paramoecium* and bacteria.

• In multicellular organisms, most cells are not in direct contact with the environment, so specialised organ systems are needed.

• *Amoeba* takes in food by forming pseudopodia (phagocytosis).

NOTE

• They have complex body structures (Option 1): Incorrect; single-celled organisms have simple, not complex, structures.

• They have a protective wall around them (Option 3): A cell wall (in some) does not explain the absence of specialised organs.

• They do not perform these functions (Option 4): Incorrect; they do perform nutrition, respiration and excretion, just without special organs.

question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding blood vessels?
option_1: Arteries are the vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.
option_2: Veins collect the blood from heart and spread it to different organs
option_3: Arteries have capillaries to prevent backflow of blood.
option_4: The smallest vessels have walls which are one-cell thick and are called veins.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arteries are the vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arteries (धमनियां) carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.

• They have thick, elastic, muscular walls to withstand the high pressure of blood pumped by the heart.

• Most arteries carry oxygenated blood (the pulmonary artery is the exception).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Veins carry blood from the organs back to the heart and have valves to prevent the backflow of blood.

• Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels, one-cell thick, where exchange of gases and nutrients occurs.

• The pulmonary vein is the exception among veins, carrying oxygenated blood.

NOTE

• Veins collect the blood from heart and spread it to different organs (Option 2): Incorrect; veins carry blood TO the heart, not away from it.

• Arteries have capillaries to prevent backflow of blood (Option 3): Incorrect; it is veins that have valves to prevent backflow.

• The smallest vessels have walls which are one-cell thick and are called veins (Option 4): Incorrect; the one-cell-thick vessels are capillaries, not veins.

question: Which of the following kings ruled during the lifetimes of both Buddha and Mahavira?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ajatashatru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ajatashatru (अजातशत्रु) of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha ruled during the lifetimes of both Gautama Buddha and Mahavira.

• He was the son of King Bimbisara and ruled around 492-460 BCE.

• He was a contemporary of both the founders of Buddhism and Jainism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ajatashatru convened the First Buddhist Council at Rajgriha after Buddha's death (mahaparinirvana).

• He founded the fort of Pataligrama (later Pataliputra), which became the Magadhan capital.

• His father Bimbisara was also a patron and contemporary of Buddha and Mahavira.

NOTE

• Chandragupta Maurya (Option 1): Founded the Maurya Empire around 322 BCE, long after Buddha and Mahavira.

• Ashok (Option 2): Mauryan emperor (3rd century BCE) who spread Buddhism after the Kalinga war, but lived much later.

• Harshavardhana (Option 4): A 7th-century CE ruler of Kannauj, several centuries after the two teachers.

question: What name did the ancient Greeks use to refer to the region around the Indus River?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indoi or Indike.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ancient Greeks (यूनानी) referred to the region around the Indus River as Indoi / Indike (इंडोई या इंडिके).

• The name derived from the river Sindhu (Indus), which the Persians pronounced as ‘Hindu’ and the Greeks as ‘Indos’.

• From this the words ‘India’ and ‘Indian’ are ultimately derived.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Persians called the land beyond the Indus Hindush / Hindu.

• The Arabs later used the term Al-Hind for the region.

• The name Bharat comes from the ancient tribe/king Bharata in Indian tradition.

NOTE

• Sindh (Option 1): The region/province around the lower Indus; the local name, not the Greek term.

• Hind (Option 3): The Persian/Arabic-derived name for India, not the Greek one.

• Bharat (Option 4): The indigenous Sanskrit name for India, unrelated to the Greeks.
